one_liner: B2B customer support platform for managing issues, accounts, and contacts.
blocker: API tokens can only be created by Admin users of an existing Pylon workspace; no free developer tier or self-serve signup is documented (site funnels to 'Book demo').

evidence.claim: API authentication is an API token sent as a Bearer header
Tokens are self-serve in the dashboard but restricted to Admin users
evidence.quote: Only Admin users can create API tokens. To learn more about Admins, see [Roles & User Management]

evidence.claim: Token generation happens in the Pylon dashboard settings
evidence.quote: Generate an API token in the [Pylon dashboard](https://app.usepylon.com/settings/api-tokens).

evidence.claim: Broad REST API spanning many resource groups
evidence.quote: bearer-authenticated interface at https://api.usepylon.com, spanning 22 documented resource groups

evidence.claim: Vendor ships an official MCP server
evidence.quote: The Pylon MCP Server exposes Pylon data to AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol

evidence.claim: MCP server is OAuth-only; no API key auth for MCP
evidence.quote: The Pylon MCP server only supports OAuth authentication. API key authentication is not currently available

notes: Name collisions in search results: getpylon.com/app.getpylon.com and docs.pylonsync.com are different products and were excluded. Official MCP at https://mcp.usepylon.com uses OAuth 2.0 (AuthKit), streamable HTTP, and must be enabled by an admin (Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server); tools cover issues, accounts, contacts, users. REST surface is broader than MCP — e.g. replying to a customer requires REST-only POST /issues/{id}/reply (per Scalekit). REST tokens are org-scoped, can be restricted by IP range or web domain. Docs are GitBook with llms.txt and .md mirrors, agent-friendly.
